ROLE: Answer a valid PINGREQ with exactly one PINGRESP queued behind any bytes already queued, keeping the session READY so later business traffic continues.

SIGNATURE.RAW: static enum broker_result handle_pingreq(struct broker *b, struct session *s)
SIGNATURE.NAME: handle_pingreq

STRUCT.NAME: struct session
STRUCT.ROLE: connected session whose queue receives PINGRESP

STRUCT.NAME: struct byte_buf
STRUCT.ROLE: queued-output buffer receiving the 2 response bytes

FUNC.NAME: session_output
FUNC.ROLE: borrow the queue that receives PINGRESP

VAR.NAME: BROKER_CONTINUE
VAR.ROLE: session stays usable after a queued PINGRESP

VAR.NAME: BROKER_CLOSE
VAR.ROLE: session could not queue its response and is closed

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: wire_encode_pingresp
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: 0 after appending exactly d0 00 (2 bytes plus the Remaining Length 0 already included); -1 for a NULL destination; -2 when the destination could not grow
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: the 2 bytes are copied into the borrowed queue; nothing is retained past the call
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: nonzero appends nothing at all, because the encoder leaves the buffer unchanged, so the caller cannot have sent a partial PINGRESP

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_output
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: borrowed pointer to the queued-output buffer of the session, NULL only for a NULL session
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: borrowed; the session keeps and eventually frees the storage, the appends only extend its length
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; the caller checks the pointer for NULL defensively

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_close_immediately
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: void; queued output is released, the descriptor is closed once and the state becomes SESSION_CLOSED (no-op when already CLOSED)
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: releases the session's queued bytes and descriptor; the broker registry entry survives until broker_reap
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; repeated calls are no-ops

LOGIC.INPUT: b: broker registry (not dereferenced; kept for signature symmetry with the other handlers). s: the READY session whose received bytes were the 2-byte PINGREQ packet already validated by wire_decode_empty(WIRE_PACKET_PINGREQ); the packet bytes have no payload, so nothing from the input buffer is needed.
LOGIC.ACTION: 1. out = session_output(s); if out is NULL, session_close_immediately(s) and return BROKER_CLOSE. 2. rc = wire_encode_pingresp(out). 3. If rc != 0: the response could not be queued (allocation failure), so the required PINGRESP cannot be sent; call session_close_immediately(s) and return BROKER_CLOSE. 4. Otherwise return BROKER_CONTINUE: exactly d0 00 was appended after every byte already queued, the session stays SESSION_READY and the next complete frame in the receive buffer is handled normally (no keepalive bookkeeping or timeout scheduling exists in this broker).
LOGIC.OUTPUT: BROKER_CONTINUE with exactly one d0 00 appended to the session output queue (never replacing already queued bytes) when encoding succeeded; BROKER_CLOSE with the session CLOSED when the output buffer could not be grown.
INVARIANTS_USED: a valid PINGREQ is answered with exactly the 2 bytes d0 00 (PINGRESP, Remaining Length 0)
queued output is only appended to, so a PINGRESP never discards an earlier queued packet
keepalive timeout scheduling is excluded from scope, so no timer is armed
a response that cannot be queued closes the connection instead of silently dropping it
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: s is non-NULL and in SESSION_READY; the caller already validated the PINGREQ fixed header (type 12, flags 0, Remaining Length 0).
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: either the session queue ends with d0 00 and the session is still READY, or the session is CLOSED with its queue released.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Single-threaded reactor; the session is not touched concurrently.

EXPECT.note: each PINGREQ appends; earlier CONNACK bytes are preserved in order
routing still works after a PINGREQ; RL = 2 + topic 3 + payload 1 = 6
